html:
A painting movement and artists' company of the Western Desert of Australia, begun at the settlement of Papunya in 1971. It brought Aboriginal dot painting to the world.

Papunya was a government settlement west of Alice Springs, where people of the Pintupi, Luritja, Warlpiri, Arrernte and other groups had been gathered from their lands. In 1971 a young art teacher, Geoffrey Bardon, encouraged senior men to paint a mural on the school wall. They painted the Honey Ant Dreaming, and soon dozens of men were painting.

The artists put on board, then canvas, designs that had been drawn in sand, on bodies and on sacred objects. They told stories of the Dreaming and of their country. Because some designs were secret, painters learned to hide or leave out sacred details, and fields of dots became a way to veil them.

In 1972 the men formed their own company, Papunya Tula Artists. Painters such as Clifford Possum Tjapaltjarri became famous. The movement spread to communities across the desert and made art an important income for Aboriginal Australia.
sum: A painting movement and artists' company of the Western Desert of Australia, begun at the settlement of Papunya in 1971. It brought Aboriginal dot painting to the world.
